messages:
Ethan (Acme): Hey team — after the new model + tokenizer cutover last night (v2-tokenizer-hybrid) our production p95/p99 for completions spiked for requests with seqlen > 2048. Users seeing timeouts and slow tails :warning:
Maya S: sorry to hear that — can you paste a failing request id and an example prompt? we need a repro to prioritize. @Jordan fyi
Ethan (Acme): request id=prod:rq_99233X, sample prompt attached (very long doc + question). Observed p95 ~ 780ms -> 2.3s and p99 up to 9s. CPU on the serving pod climbs and then we see repeated KV-cache misses.
Ethan (Acme): curl snippet for repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' \\n  -d '{"model": "v2-tokenizer-hybrid", "input": "<long doc>...", "max_tokens": 256}'
```
deploy-bot: model v2-tokenizer-hybrid rolled out to prod at 2025-11-03T03:08:02Z (canary->100%)
Jordan (SRE): looking at traces — requests with long-prefix show many KV cache invalidations and repeated handler reinstantiation. the runtime is repeatedly evicting KV shards around sequence boundary ~2048-2300. batch latency also balloons.
Liam R: we added a tokenizer variant that emits extra tokens for punctuation and CJK normalization. avg token count increased ~+28% on some corpora — that could push requests over internal seq thresholds and trigger different exec-paths/kernels. also a small change to prefix-hash changed cache key boundaries.
Sarah K: repro script I used locally:
```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/repro_longctx.py --model v2-tokenizer-hybrid --seq 2200 --prompt-file tests/fixtures/long_doc.txt
# shows p95 jump and repeated kvcache misses
```
Maya S: ok steps from support side — throttle big seq requests, route Acme traffic to v1, get quick root-cause. Ethan — can we failover Acme to v1 while we debug?
Ethan (Acme): yes please, we need baseline SLA. routing to v1 should be fine for now :thumbsup:
Jordan (SRE): quick mitigation options:
• rollback tokenizer change (revert to v1 tokenization)
• partial traffic split (route >2k seq to v1)
• increase kvcache shards on the runtime to reduce eviction pressure
• disable aggressive batching for long requests (reduce batch window)
Liam R: short-term I'd prefer splitting traffic + bump kvcache shards. patch to tokenizer is higher-risk for night. Also I can push a config to stop mapping certain unicode normalizations which caused token blowup.
Maya S: I'm going to open an internal incident and request a canary rollback. tagging @Jordan and @Liam for infra/runtime changes.
Jordan (SRE): digging into logs — here's a snippet from the runtime showing repeated shard eviction and re-keying:
```
[2025-11-03T03:12:11Z] kvcache: shard 7 evict count++ -> evicting ephemeral entries for request prod:rq_99233X
[2025-11-03T03:12:11Z] runtime: cold-enter for handler id=0x7fa, initializing kv map for seq-boundary=2300
[2025-11-03T03:12:12Z] runtime: batch windowsize 32ms -> triggered continuous batching backoff
```
Sarah K: also noticed tokenizer on v2 can split some tokens into 2-3 tokens vs v1, so ops multiply. We should add an evaluation metric during onboarding that flags >10% token inflation on a customer's dataset.
Maya S: starting rollback canary now — routing 10% -> v1 for Acme and pausing further v2 rollouts.
deploy-bot: routing rule updated: route 90% traffic to v2-tokenizer-hybrid, 10% to v1-tokenizer at 2025-11-03T03:22:05Z
Ethan (Acme): after the reroute p95 dropped to ~420ms for those requests and p99 down from 9s to ~600ms. still some tails but much better.
Jordan (SRE): pushing kvcache shard bump to affected cluster (increase shard_count 8->12) and enabling prefix pinning for long requests. rolling config now.
Liam R: deployed a hotfix to tokenizer mapping to avoid the specific CJK normalization that caused token multiplication. This will be included in a proper v2.1 — hotfix is conservative.
Maya S: can we add an immediate guardrail: reject or require explicit header for sequence length > 3k with warning? that would prevent customers from accidentally hitting the pathological path while we finalize fixes.
Sarah K: I'll add an automated check to the model onboarding CI to compare tokenization delta per-customer dataset and block merges with >15% inflation.
Ethan (Acme): Confirming: after the mix of canary routing + shard bump + hotfix we saw p99 back down to ~720ms and error rates normalized. Thanks for the quick response.
Maya S: filing follow-up runbook and postmortem action items:
- add token-inflation gating in onboarding CI
- improve kvcache metrics/alerts for seq-boundary evictions
- refine rollout policy to keep tokenizer changes in canary for longer on corpora with heavy CJK
- customer-facing note + opt-in for tokenizer variants
Jordan (SRE): creating infra ticket for kvcache shard autoscaling and a short-term dashboard for eviction rates.
Liam R: I'll prepare a more thorough eval report and a smaller tokenization patch for v2.1.
Ethan (Acme): appreciate the fast turnaround — will monitor and report back if we see any residual tail.
Maya S: closing the immediate escalation. will attach logs/traces to the incident and follow up in the postmortem channel. :white_check_mark:
